part: Local privacy gate plugin for text PDFs (F084)
problem: An in-house plugin is built and proven before attachments go on, to refuse a PDF that looks like a bank statement or tax form; it cannot check photos or scanned PDFs, and whether it can see PDF text at all is untested. The card calls it a condition Tony set, but the records show it only as a proposal inside an open question, and Tony's answer on 11 Oct was to apply for Zero Data Retention.
checked: Card how, caveats 1-2, unverified 5, safety ('a tripwire for text PDFs, not a guarantee'), depends_on 1 and the round 2 history line ('the condition Tony set'). Fact sheet: Tony agreed to apply for Zero Data Retention; no request for a gate is recorded. The project's 9 Oct decision note lists 'attachments on, gated on a privacy hook' under decisions still open, and frame.decisions shows the gate as the assistant's recommendation. Roadmap: no rule asks for screening a parent's own attachments. G015 (decided 11 Oct) sends each parent's whole inbox, money and tax-form mail included, to the same cloud model with no such screen. The card's one source for input filtering (an OWASP page) is marked unchecked.

proposal.text: Do you want Happy to refuse text PDFs that look like bank statements or tax forms before attachments are switched on? Default: no gate. Switch includeAttachments on with audio understanding left off, add one AGENTS.md line and tell both parents not to send statements, tax forms or (until Zero Data Retention is approved) medical bills, and keep the single hidden-instructions eval case.

loses: A tripwire that would catch a text-PDF statement or tax form sent by mistake. Photos and scans were never covered.

part: 'A local classifier could later replace the pattern match' (decision_evaluate with the on-device ONNX plugin)
problem: The card keeps a later upgrade path for the gate: an experimental on-device classifier with a 512-token input limit and a threshold tuned on a labelled set of the family's own documents. Nobody asked for it and no card needs it.
checked: Card caveat 7 and the adds note from OCL-14; removed.json row for OCL-14 ('a building block that no card needs yet'); frame.decisions_intro says the local-classifier decision is gone because nothing is gated on it; the fact sheet has nothing on it.

proposal.text: Delete the caveat. If the gate is kept it stays a plain pattern match; a classifier is looked at only if the pattern match is seen to fail in use.

part: Voice memos in and spoken replies out for the two adults, placed in wave A
problem: The card's own first caveat says a parent can already dictate a text on the iPhone, so for the two adults this is a convenience, yet it sits in wave A with three installs, a live privacy test and twelve open checks. The roadmap planned voice memos for the kids' milestone, and the kids agent is parked under Later.
checked: Card caveat 1, value 2, depends_on (whisper.cpp, ffmpeg and a model file; a first live test), the twelve entries under unverified. Roadmap: voice memos are an M5b (kids) deliverable, and 'Kids voice' is the only voice decision in section 9 marked By: You. Config repo: the includeAttachments comment says voice memos arrive in M5. Fact sheet: Tony's own examples of wanted capabilities do not include voice for the adults. r7.json: F072 (kids) is 'later'; only optional parts of AUT-06 and OCL-01 use F003.

proposal.text: Move F003 to Later, next to the kids agent it was planned for. Wave A keeps only the line already in F002 that leaves audio understanding off. If Tony wants it sooner, ship transcription only, with no spoken replies.

loses: Voice memos to Happy and audio replies for the parents until then; the read-aloud option in the practice quiz (AUT-06) and the local engine option for Talk (OCL-01) wait too.

part: 'Later step: a natural voice by one of three documented routes'
problem: The card plans a second, nicer voice and keeps three ways to get it, one of them a local speech server with its own background job, plus a decision on which to pick. Nobody has asked for a nicer voice, and nobody has heard the built-in one yet.
checked: Card how, caveat 6 (a third-party package from a 0.0.x project, a loopback server with its own launchd job, a model download; none installed), depends_on 3, unverified 5 and 8. Fact sheet: nothing on voice quality. Roadmap: names only 'a local TTS command'.

proposal.text: Remove the later step, its caveat and its decision from the card. Spoken replies, if built at all, use the built-in macOS voice; a nicer voice is researched only if a parent asks for one.

loses: nothing now; the three routes would be looked up again if ever wanted

part: Granting the message tool, re-opening the same-channel send switch, then an in-house hook to pin recipients
problem: Today no parent's agent can send anywhere except the chat it is answering, by config alone; the card opens that up and then writes an in-house hook to close it again, so Happy can pass notes between two adults who can text each other. Saying yes also lets one parent's agent put what it holds in front of the other parent, which the card itself says the one-data-domain-per-person rule would not allow.
checked: Config repo: tools.message.crossContext has both switches false, and each parent's agent denies group:messaging. Roadmap section 1b 'Replies' row (no sends into other conversations; scheduled jobs deliver only to their owner) and section 9 'Family data domains', By: You. Card caveat 1 ('a small convenience'), caveat 3, depends_on 2, safety. Installed tool-permissions.md:35-58 (the two switches; they do not confine operator CLI sends). r7.json dependents in waves A and B: CRT-04 needs only a notice, and F018's alerts are operator-created jobs, both with targets the operator writes; CRT-10 and MKT-06 use only the optional relay. Fact sheet: Tony has not asked for note passing.

proposal.text: Leave the live config as it is: no message tool on any agent and both switches off. Notices and scheduled texts keep going out from jobs and host scripts whose targets the generator writes from family.json5. Build the fail-closed hook only for a tool that lets an agent name a destination: the scheduling tool if F007 is confirmed, and the email tool in F049.

loses: 'Tell Jordan...' and 'ask Jordan...' through Happy, and any text an agent composes to the other parent or the group from outside the chat it is in. The parents text each other directly.

part: Ask-and-relay step (G010): pending-requests table, a before_dispatch plugin for a bare yes or no, a one-shot reminder and expiry
problem: To carry 'can you do Thursday pickup?' to the other parent and bring back the yes, the card adds a database table, a second plugin that checks incoming texts for a bare yes or no, and timed jobs for a nudge and an expiry. The card itself says the gain over the parents texting each other is only tracking, one reminder and an expiry.
checked: Card how, caveat 1, unverified 4 (no plugin-side send call was found, so the relay may not be buildable as written) and unverified 6 ('judgement, not sourced'). Its one outside source describes a co-parenting app. Fact sheet: no request from Tony, and whether Jordan wants any of this is unstated. r7.json: only optional add-ons in CRT-10 and MKT-06 use the step; it also pulls in F031 and F007.

proposal.text: Remove the relay step from the card and the 'ask-and-relay' add-ons from CRT-10 and MKT-06. A parent who wants an answer from the other parent texts them, or asks in the parents' group chat.

loses: A tracked ask with one nudge and an expiry, relayed through Happy.

part: Scheduling tool granted to each parent's agent, plus a hook to police it, for 'remind me at 4:30'
problem: To make 'remind me at 4:30' work, the agent that holds a parent's notes is given OpenClaw's scheduling tool, which OpenClaw says to keep away from agents that read outside content, and a hook is then needed to make that safe. As things stand only Tony could use it, and the card says the phone's own Reminders app and Siri already do plain timers.
checked: Card how, safety, depends_on, caveat 1 (the card marks the Siri comparison as not sourced; Apple's Reminders page is among its sources). Installed hardened-baseline.md:38 (senders who are not command owners cannot use the scheduling tool whatever the config says) and tool-permissions.md:21-28 (deny cron by default where untrusted content is handled). Config repo: one command owner; group:automation denied on both parents' agents. Fact sheet: 'No need' to add Jordan to the command list; no statement that timed texts from Happy are wanted. Roadmap: lists 'Reminders' as a skill of each parent's agent, with no design.

proposal.text: Timed reminder texts from Happy would work for you only, unless Jordan is made a command owner (a bigger grant than the one you declined), and the phone already sets a timed reminder by voice. Build it in wave A anyway? Default: defer. Keep the scheduling tool off every agent and build no hook for it; one AGENTS.md line has Happy say it cannot set timers yet. Revisit with F010 (wave B), the first card where a reminder comes out of something Happy read. If yes: build it for Tony only, with the hook limited to add and update.

loses: 'Remind me' by text, and listing and cancelling reminders by text. The day-before reminder offers in F010, F051, CRT-10, CRT-11 and CRT-13 wait with it.

part: Refusing update, run and remove on jobs another agent created, and trimming the job list
problem: The card proposes a second layer in the hook so one parent's agent cannot see or change the other's reminders or the generated jobs. Only Tony's agent would hold the tool, and Tony is the operator who can already read and change every job.
checked: Card safety (last three sentences) and caveat 3; installed managing-jobs.md:79 (a command owner's agent can manage any job) and the same page's note that each such change is written to the scheduler's admin log; config repo (one command owner); roadmap section 1b ('You ... can read every person's data') and fact sheet ('No strict isolation from the operator'). No roadmap rule asks for job-level separation from the operator.

proposal.text: If reminders are built, the hook checks only add and update: the text goes to the asker, no web address, an empty tool list. No per-job ownership check and no list trimming unless a second command owner is ever added.

loses: A guard against a planted instruction making Tony's agent switch off or edit another job; such a change is still recorded in the scheduler's admin log.

problem: The name, description and build are written for a shared family calendar on Google. Tony has never said the family keeps a shared calendar, or on which service, and ten other cards read the calendar through this one.
checked: Fact sheet ('Never stated': which calendar the family shares and whether both parents use it); config repo family.json5 records no calendar account; card depends_on 1 still says 'Google or iCloud ... still open'; frame.decisions 3. The only backing for Google is indirect: both parents use Gmail. r7.json lists ten cards that depend on F009.

proposal.text: Do you and Jordan keep one shared calendar, and is it a Google calendar? Default: yes, Google, since both of you use Gmail. If it is iCloud or there is none, this card and the calendar part of the briefs wait. Either way drop the iCloud branch from the card: it needs the OpenClaw Mac app, which the plan recommends not installing in this batch.

part: Etiquette (G014): 'on it', 'cancel that' through the subagents tool, concurrency caps
problem: The card specifies an acknowledgement, a cancel phrase and concurrency limits for slow lookups before any lookup has been seen to run slowly. The cancel phrase means giving each parent's agent one more tool, and two parents will not reach the default limit of eight lookups at once.
checked: Card how and unverified 8-9 ('nothing on the current stack runs longer than about 20 seconds'; 'the model can skip them'). Installed subagents.md:14 (a finished helper reports back by default), nesting.md:24 (default caps and a spawn time-limit setting), subagents/operations.md 'Stopping' (/stop in the requester chat cancels its running helpers). Config repo: the subagents tool is denied on both parents' agents today. Fact sheet and roadmap: nothing on this.

proposal.text: Keep one setting, a time limit on the hand-off, and the built-in report when the helper finishes. No subagents tool on the parents' agents, no concurrency tuning, no scripted acknowledgement. Add an 'on it' line only if real lookups turn out slow enough to confuse.

loses: 'Cancel that' in plain words for a running lookup. Tony's built-in stop still ends it; for Jordan the lookup ends at its time limit.

part: Answer rules (F022): the 30-day staleness flag and the four-way fact-check verdict with two or three dated sources
problem: On top of 'give the link and when it was fetched', the helper's instructions carry a fixed fact-check format and a rule to flag pages older than 30 days. The card records the 30-day figure and the link cap as house choices with no source, and says nothing enforces any of it.
checked: Card how, unverified 6-7 ('a prompt rule the model can ignore'; 'house choices with no source'), adds from F025 and F026. Roadmap M3 sets one answer rule only: prices from live tool results with a timestamp, links and not bookings. Fact sheet: nothing.

proposal.text: One AGENTS.md rule for the helper: give the link and the time fetched, give a price or date only if it came from a fetched page, and say 'could not verify' when a page could not be read. Drop the verdict format, the 30-day flag and the link cap; add a rule back when a real answer shows the need.

loses: A uniform true, false, mixed or unclear shape for fact checks, and an automatic 'this page is old' note.

part: 'host-side helpers that take a URL (... watcher scripts) need their own scheme, host and resolved-address checks'
problem: The card asks every host script that takes a web address to carry its own home-network checks, and names the watcher scripts. The watchers' addresses are written by Tony in config, not chosen by a model or a web page, so that check has nothing to stop.
checked: Card caveat 4; F018 how in r7.json ('all are operator-created host command jobs' with no model call); roadmap section 5 (the risk is content a model reads steering a tool). The check does make sense for a script that fetches a link passed in from chat or by a model (the print download in F080, the summarize wrapper in F020).

proposal.text: 'Host-side helpers that fetch an address supplied in chat or by a model (the summarize wrapper, the print download) need their own scheme, host and resolved-address checks; scripts whose addresses Tony writes in config (the watchers) do not.'

part: 'the Reminders lists the family already shares'
problem: The card, and the plan's recommendation that Jordan's reminders go through 'the shared Reminders list', assume the parents already share an Apple Reminders list. Tony has never said so.
checked: Fact sheet ('Never stated': whether the family uses Apple Reminders lists or a shared grocery list); config repo family.json5 has no such record; frame.decisions 3 recommendation; card depends_on 1.

proposal.text: Do you and Jordan share an Apple Reminders list today (groceries or to-dos) that you would want Happy to add to? Default if not: take F030 out of wave A and remove the recommendation that Jordan's reminders go through it.

part: In-house Reminders plugin built in wave A
problem: A host-side plugin is built in the first wave, but the card says Siri already adds a single item and that the bridge earns its place only for items that come out of a recipe, a meal plan or a flyer. Those uses sit in wave C (F033, value 2), and the one thing the card says must be proven first has not been tried.
checked: Card caveat 2, description ('the first thing to prove'), unverified 1-2, depends_on 3. r7.json: only F033 (wave C) and the undo in G006 (wave B) depend on F030. Installed skills/apple-reminders/SKILL.md (it drives remindctl from a shell, which the sandboxed agents do not have, so a small plugin is the right shape once the bridge is needed).

proposal.text: Before writing anything: in happy's desktop session, join one shared list and run remindctl by hand to add and tick off an item, then look at both phones. If it does not sync, drop the card. If it does, build the three-verb plugin together with the first card that needs it (F033), not in wave A.

loses: Adding several items to the shared list by text until then; each parent can still tell their phone.
